list.name: Basic Electronics & Robotics Foundation
list.desc: Learn electronics and robotics fundamentals with hands-on circuit building.
list.longDesc: This program introduces children to the fascinating world of electronics through a fully hands-on, project-based journey. Rather than focusing on complicated theory, students learn by doing — building real circuits, wiring their own gadgets and watching their creations come to life. Over 9 progressive modules, they will construct 20 exciting projects including automatic night lamps, motion detectors, and solar-powered devices, gaining practical engineering confidence.
modules: Module 1: Getting Started with Electronics & Safety
Module 2: Understanding Electricity & Circuits (Voltage, Current, Resistance)
Module 3: Building Circuits on Breadboards (Wiring Diagrams)
Module 4: Working with Everyday Components (LEDs, Switches, Buzzers)
Module 5: Sensors & Smart Electronics (Infrared, Temperature, Light, Moisture)
Module 6: Motors & Motion (Fan speeds, Direction, Moving vehicle base)
Module 7: Advanced Components (Capacitors, Diodes, Transistors, Relays)
Module 8: Timing & Control Systems (Integrated Circuits, 555 Timer, Traffic lights)
Module 9: Renewable Energy & Capstone Projects (Solar panels, Solar cars)
list.imageAlt: Hands using tweezers and a screwdriver to solder components onto a circuit board with a heat sink

list.name: Quad Bot – ESP32 Smart Robotics
list.desc: Build and program a four-legged walking robot using ESP32 with wireless control.
list.longDesc: This smart robotics program focuses on legged locomotion and modern wireless integrations. Taught using the ESP32 platform, students will build a four-legged walking robot. They will cover five advanced project configurations: driving the robot via Infrared remote controller signals, implementing ultrasonic obstacle avoidance, configuring Wi-Fi hosting server control from smartphones, and programming voice-command operations and wireless motion-gesture glove controls (using the MPU6050 sensor).
modules: Module 1: Quad Bot Chassis Assembly, Mechanical Linkages & Servo Calibration
Module 2: IR Remote Control Smart Robot (ESP32 remote signal decoding)
Module 3: Obstacle Avoidance Smart Robot (Ultrasonic sound wave navigation)
Module 4: Wi-Fi Controlled Smart Robot (Smartphone web server integration)
Module 5: Voice & Speech Controlled Smart Robot (Speech command algorithms)
Module 6: Gesture & Motion Controlled Smart Robot (MPU6050 wireless glove control)
list.imageAlt: A student working on a laptop connected to an electronics testing rig with wiring harnesses in a lab

list.name: Gyro Bot – STM32 Autonomous Robotics
list.desc: Master autonomous self-balancing and navigation using STM32 microcontrollers and gyroscopic sensors.
list.longDesc: An advanced, embedded systems and control engineering curriculum built on the STM32 microcontroller and Yahboom SBR-STM32 platform. Over 10 modules, students learn professional workflows (Keil MDK, STM32CubeIDE, and VSCode) and embedded C programming. They will implement PID control algorithms,Complementary/Kalman filtering, app controls, K210 AI computer vision (for colour, QR-code, and number tracking), Lidar spatial navigation (obstacle avoidance and wall-tracking), and trace schematics to understand PCB hardware design.
modules: Module 1: Getting Started & Professional STM32 Toolchain (Keil MDK & CubeIDE)
Module 2: STM32 Embedded Programming Foundations (GPIO, Interrupts, Timers, PWM, I2C, SPI)
Module 3: Actuators, DC Motors, Wheel Encoders & MPU6050 Gyroscopic Readouts
Module 4: Control Theory & PID Tuning (Position vs. Incremental PID, Cascade loops)
Module 5: The Science of Dynamic Self-Balancing (MPU6050 DMP, Kalman & Complementary fusion)
Module 6: Autonomous Behaviours & Bluetooth Smartphone App Controls
Module 7: Intelligent Perception & K210 Edge AI Vision (QR-code, Colour, & Object Recognition)
Module 8: Lidar Navigation (Obstacle avoidance, Guarding, Patrolling, Wall-tracking)
Module 9: LQR Optimal Control Theory, Balance Mathematics & Hardware Circuit Analysis
Module 10: Capstone Project: Autonomous Driving Self-Balancing Smart Car
list.imageAlt: Close-up of a green microcontroller board with colorful jumper wires on a workbench

roboticsSports.title: Robotics Sports Training
roboticsSports.tagline: Runs in parallel with the core curriculum, throughout the program.
roboticsSports.overview: Alongside the core electronics and robotics courses, every student trains across a full lineup of competitive robotics sports. Each event builds real-world engineering skill under real-world pressure — designing, building, tuning, testing, and competing — while developing teamwork, strategic thinking, and the confidence that comes from competing on a live field. New events are added to the program over time as the curriculum grows.
roboticsSports.moreEventsNote: …with more competitive robotics events added to the program over time.

events.name: Robo Soccer
events.description: Team-based robots battle to control the ball and score goals, blending mechanical design with live strategy and driving skill.

events.name: Robo Race
events.description: Each student tunes and drives their own robot for the fastest clean lap, testing motor control and driving precision.

events.name: Robo Sumo
events.description: Two robots go head-to-head in a ring, using power, traction, and smart tactics to push the opponent out.

events.name: Line Follower
events.description: Autonomous robots read and follow a marked path using sensors, competing on speed and accuracy.

events.name: Maze Solver
events.description: Robots autonomously map an unknown maze and find the shortest path to the goal, building on sensing and algorithmic logic.

events.name: Rover Challenge
events.description: All-terrain rovers navigate rough, unpredictable ground to complete objective-based tasks, testing mechanical toughness and driving skill.

events.name: Robo War (Combat Robotics)
events.description: Armored robots battle head-to-head with weapons like spinners and flippers until one is disabled — the flagship event, and the exact discipline DS Inventek's founders won their World Championship in.

events.name: Drone Racing
events.description: Students pilot small racing drones through timed obstacle courses, mastering flight control and precision piloting.

events.name: Submarine (Underwater ROV)
events.description: Students build and pilot a tethered underwater robot through underwater tasks, learning buoyancy control and remote operation.

events.name: Pick and Place
events.description: Students build and program a robotic arm to accurately pick up and place objects at target locations — a core skill in industrial automation.
